articles.title: A matter of definition : variation in treatment success of fracture-related infections.
articles.authors: Reinert N, Poggioli A, Metsemakers WJ, Clauss M, Kuehl R, Morgenstern M, et al.
articles.population: Adult patients undergoing surgery for fracture-related infections
articles.outcomes: Treatment success at one year using seven different outcome definitions, ranging from no infection persistence (95.5% success) to combined criteria of bone healing and no infection with no unplanned surgery (39.3% success in non-healed fractures)
articles.take_home: How doctors measure success after treating bone infections varies greatly, with success rates ranging from 60.7% to 95.5% in the same group of patients depending on which definition is used. Patients with bones that did not heal had much lower success rates, especially when multiple criteria like bone healing, infection control and avoiding further surgery were required together.

articles.title: Non-medical surgical delay increases one-year mortality following hip fracture.
articles.authors: Busby C, Nightingale J, Deacon C, Deakin D, Valdes A, Ollivere BJ, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 60 years and over admitted with fragility femoral fracture
articles.outcomes: All-cause one-year mortality and length of stay
articles.take_home: Patients whose hip fracture surgery was delayed beyond 36 hours due to lack of surgical capacity had a 20% higher risk of death within one year compared to those operated on sooner. The risk increased further with longer delays, suggesting that getting patients to theatre quickly is important for survival.

articles.title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists are associated with improved 90-day outcomes after total hip and knee arthroplasty : a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Rudran B, Little CDJ, Palmer AJR, Judge A, Carli A, Price AJ, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip or knee replacement, many with type 2 diabetes or obesity
articles.sample_size: 96,356 patients across 10 studies (30,350 hip replacements and 66,606 knee replacements)
articles.outcomes: 90-day surgical complications (infection, wound problems, fracture, blood clots, nerve injury), medical complications, hospital readmission, revision surgery rates, length of stay and healthcare costs
articles.take_home: Patients taking GLP-1 receptor agonist medications (used for diabetes and weight loss) had fewer complications and readmissions within 90 days of hip or knee replacement, particularly after hip replacement. The evidence quality was low to moderate, so more high-quality research is needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Use of neurolytic nerve blocks and mortality in nonoperative management of hip fracture patients : a nationwide population study in the Netherlands.
articles.authors: van Bremen HE, Lommerse MI, Hegeman JH, Schuijt HJ, Kallewaard JW, Wijnen HH, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 70 years and older with hip fractures treated nonoperatively
articles.outcomes: Mortality at 7 days, 30 days, 3 months and 6 months
articles.take_home: Patients with hip fractures who received neurolytic nerve blocks had lower mortality in the first week, but higher mortality by three months. These blocks are increasingly used in the Netherlands for very frail patients who are not having surgery.

articles.title: Outcomes after Retrograde Intramedullary Nailing of 33C Femur Fractures.
articles.authors: Obey MR, Payne C, Falgons CG, Hunter NB, Wright AP, Eastman JG, et al.
articles.population: Patients with complete articular distal femur fractures treated with open reduction and retrograde intramedullary nailing
articles.outcomes: Radiographic alignment (aLDFA and aPDFA), articular reduction quality, reoperation rates, and fracture union rates
articles.take_home: This surgical technique for complex femur fractures achieved excellent results, with nearly all fractures healing properly and bone alignment maintained. About 15% of patients needed further surgery, mostly for minor issues like implant irritation, with only 4% requiring major unplanned operations.

articles.title: A comprehensive review of trauma transfers to a rural pediatric trauma center.
articles.authors: Koenen M, Sang HI, Gorra A, Ryckman J
articles.study_type: Retrospective review of trauma registry data
articles.population: Children under 15 years old transferred to a rural Level 2 paediatric trauma centre
articles.outcomes: Identification of transfer patterns and diagnoses associated with potentially avoidable transfers; falls were the most common mechanism; concussions and skull fractures without bleeding were often avoidable transfers
articles.take_home: About 1 in 10 transfers to this paediatric trauma centre may have been avoidable, particularly for minor head injuries and cases with no injury found. Improving communication between local hospitals and the trauma centre could help reduce unnecessary transfers.

articles.title: Combined C5 and CD14 inhibition balances immunological miRNA responses after multiple trauma in pigs.
articles.authors: Groven RVM, Mert U, Greven J, He Z, Zhou N, Poeze M, et al.
articles.population: Pigs undergoing multiple trauma with intramedullary nailing
articles.outcomes: MicroRNA and mRNA expression at fracture site and in plasma, lung and liver; inflammatory and anti-inflammatory markers
articles.take_home: Blocking two immune pathways (C5 and CD14) together reduced harmful inflammatory responses after multiple trauma whilst preserving bone healing processes in this pig model. The treatment also reduced inflammatory markers circulating in the blood and reaching the lungs and liver.

articles.title: Evacuation of hemothorax during SSRF: Does the technique influence the outcome?
articles.authors: Sutori D, White TW, Molnar TF, Harmati IA, Uri I, Zsoldos P, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort analysis of prospectively collected data
articles.population: Patients with rib fractures and hemothorax undergoing surgical stabilization
articles.outcomes: Primary: chest tube duration. Secondary: pneumonia, mortality, ICU length of stay, hospital length of stay, 30-day readmission, mechanical ventilation days
articles.take_home: Video-assisted thoracic surgery resulted in shorter chest tube duration compared to blind irrigation, but both techniques had similar outcomes for pneumonia, mortality, hospital stay and readmission rates. The choice of technique did not significantly affect broader clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Occupational and sociodemographic inequalities in fire, heat and hot substance-related injuries among working-age adults: A Global Burden of Disease 2021 analysis.
articles.authors: Xiang B, Li F, Yi Z, Zhong X
articles.study_type: Global epidemiological analysis using Global Burden of Disease 2021 data
articles.population: Working-age adults aged 20-54 years across 204 countries
articles.outcomes: Prevalence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) from fire, heat and hot substance-related injuries; associations with socioeconomic development and occupational exposure
articles.take_home: Globally, fire and heat injuries in working-age adults have declined since 1990, but large inequalities remain between regions. Occupational injuries are a major cause in developing countries, while poor burn care systems drive excess deaths and disability in lower-income settings.

articles.title: Prioritizing harm reduction in instant delivery crashes: Predictors of pedestrian injury severity and targeted interventions.
articles.authors: Yan X, Zhang X, Ye X, Chen J, Wang T, Du M, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective analysis of court verdicts using Hierarchical Generalized Ordered Probit modelling
articles.population: Pedestrians involved in instant delivery crashes that resulted in litigation
articles.outcomes: Predictors of pedestrian injury severity (graded by disability level); identified older age (65-74 years) and motorbike involvement as strong predictors of higher-grade disability, whilst female pedestrians and winter conditions correlated with lower severity
articles.take_home: This study of legal cases involving delivery crashes found that older pedestrians and those hit by motorbikes faced more severe injuries, whilst female pedestrians and winter conditions were linked to less severe outcomes. The findings suggest that age-adapted infrastructure and motorbike regulations could help reduce harm, although the results only apply to serious cases that went to court.

articles.title: Low incidence of severe cardiac complications in traumatic sternal fractures: Rethinking routine rhythm monitoring.
articles.authors: Klei DS, Verstegen SBH, Ahmetagic D, van Osch D, van Wessem KJP
articles.population: Adult blunt trauma patients with traumatic sternal fractures
articles.sample_size: 350 patients (113 with suspected blunt cardiac injury)
articles.outcomes: Severe cardiac complications (sustained ventricular tachycardia, high-degree atrioventricular block, need for cardiac surgery, primary cardiac arrest, or death from cardiac cause); clinically relevant cardiac findings requiring treatment or follow-up
articles.take_home: Severe cardiac complications after sternal fractures are very rare, occurring in only 1.8% of patients with suspected heart injury. The study suggests that routine heart rhythm monitoring may not be necessary for all patients and that admission decisions should be based on overall clinical condition rather than cardiac monitoring alone.

articles.title: Navigating the antithrombotic challenge in hip-fracture care: A framework to avoid delays and optimise patient outcomes.
articles.authors: Marta M, Costa L, Paulo Moreira J, Araujo F
articles.population: Older adults with hip fractures on chronic antithrombotic therapy
articles.outcomes: Perioperative management approach, surgical timing, haemostatic safety, functional recovery and survival
articles.take_home: Hip fracture patients on anticlotting medicines should have surgery as soon as possible, ideally within 24 hours, rather than waiting for drugs to clear from their system. A practical framework using active blood tests and flexible anaesthesia choices can help surgeons operate safely without unnecessary delays.

articles.title: Abdominal trauma and laparotomy in wartime civilian and military casualties: A National Registry Study.
articles.authors: Gendler S, Sarfaty E, Talmy T, Givon A, Schrier I
articles.population: Civilian and military casualties with abdominal trauma during the Swords of Iron War
articles.sample_size: 561 patients with abdominal injuries (140 underwent laparotomy)
articles.outcomes: Mortality, ICU admission, rehabilitation discharge, and need for laparotomy
articles.take_home: One quarter of people with abdominal war injuries needed surgery. Certain types of injury to the bowel, colon, liver and major blood vessels were strong predictors of who would need surgery.

articles.title: Evaluation of erectile dysfunction following pelvic fractures: A retrospective analysis.
articles.authors: Tabassum A, Kruijning M, Wong J, Jenkins L, Langcake M
articles.population: Male patients with traumatic pelvic fractures
articles.outcomes: Incidence of erectile dysfunction and associated risk factors
articles.take_home: Erectile dysfunction occurred in about 5% of male patients after pelvic fractures, with having an embolization procedure being the main risk factor. The study suggests doctors should routinely check for this complication and refer patients to urology specialists early, especially those who have had embolization.

articles.title: Diagnostic evaluation of delayed flexion-extension radiographs after blunt cervical spine trauma: A prospective study.
articles.authors: Emin L, Lafont C, Ravaillault S, Gardeton L, Lehuede A, Geay C, et al.
articles.population: Alert patients with persistent neck pain after blunt cervical spine trauma, with normal neurological examination and normal initial static imaging
articles.sample_size: 303 patients referred to delayed dynamic radiography pathway; 24 patients who had surgery for unstable cervical injury diagnosed acutely
articles.outcomes: Number of unstable cervical ligamentous injuries identified on delayed flexion-extension radiographs; clinical and radiological features of surgically treated unstable injuries
articles.take_home: Delayed flexion-extension radiographs did not find any surgically important cervical spine injuries in patients with normal nerve examination and normal initial imaging. The study suggests this routine test may not be needed and that initial assessment with nerve examination and CT scanning is more important.

articles.title: Despite lower fracture rates, homeless patients have worse outcomes after geriatric ground-level falls: an analysis of National Trauma Data Bank.
articles.authors: Wang K, Sirilan A, Zach R, Jia A, Agarwal N, Dehghan N
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national trauma database
articles.population: Adults aged 50 years and older hospitalised for ground-level falls in the United States
articles.outcomes: Fracture rates, length of hospital stay of 7 days or more, ICU admission, complications, in-hospital mortality, and discharge location
articles.take_home: Homeless patients had fewer fractures than housed patients after falls, but experienced worse overall outcomes including longer hospital stays, more ICU admissions and more complications. Homelessness itself was found to be independently linked to worse outcomes even after accounting for age and medical complexity.

articles.title: Moral injury in orthopaedic surgery: Distinguishing burnout from system-level ethical conflict.
articles.authors: Saad J, Aboukar M, Quick JC, Saleh A, Saleh KJ
articles.outcomes: Moral injury, burnout, depression, suicidal ideation, professional identity and trust, surgeon wellbeing
articles.take_home: Orthopaedic surgeons experience a specific type of psychological harm called moral injury, which goes beyond burnout and happens when they cannot provide timely care, are pressured into ethically conflicting decisions, or witness preventable suffering. This framework helps distinguish moral injury from burnout to better support surgeon wellbeing.

articles.title: Riding the shockwave: Escalating spine injuries from electric micromobility devices in the United States.
articles.authors: Tannoury T, El-Hajj N, Dhunna DP, Khan RR, Ryali R, Zhou OT, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective longitudinal analysis of national surveillance data
articles.population: Patients presenting to emergency departments with spine injuries caused by electric micromobility devices
articles.sample_size: 2699 patients with electric micromobility-related spine injuries between 2015 and 2024
articles.outcomes: Spine injury types (fractures, contusions, sprains, nerve injuries), patient demographics, yearly injury trends, and discharge status
articles.take_home: Spine injuries from electric scooters, hoverboards and skateboards have increased dramatically over the past decade, with fractures being the most common injury type. Males and adults aged 25 and over are at higher risk, and more public awareness about safe use of these devices is needed to prevent injuries.

articles.title: Progressive enhancement in cadaver-based trauma surgery simulation: A 22-course longitudinal evaluation of partecipant-reported realism, learning and satisfaction.
articles.authors: Mongardini FM, Bellanova G, Calderale S, Ceci F, Chiantera V, Cipriani B, et al.
articles.population: Surgeons and surgical trainees attending advanced trauma surgery courses
articles.sample_size: 176 participants across 22 course editions from 2018 to 2025
articles.outcomes: Participant-reported realism, learning, satisfaction and comparison with other training modalities, measured on 10-point scales
articles.take_home: Using more realistic cadaver models for trauma training, progressing from non-perfused to perfused and mechanically ventilated bodies, resulted in higher participant ratings for realism, learning and satisfaction. The biggest improvement came from adding vascular perfusion to the models.
